From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:03:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: increased latency + 503s across our traffic (logs attached)

Quick triage notes after looking at traces and policy engine logs:
- Root cause appears to be an unintended overlap between the per-tenant burst window and the new capacity-reserve safety valve we rolled for reserved pools last week.
- Fairshare algorithm is treating Eidos as high-burst but low-credit after the reserve kick-in; that combination is producing sharp headroom clamps leading to request drops (503) and elevated tail latency due to queuing.
- The policy diff attached shows we tightened the reserve bucket and reduced burst credits for tenants that exceed a short-window QPS threshold. Eidos’ traffic pattern (short high-frequency spikes followed by steady sustained load) now hits both checks and loses prefetched KV-cache entries during retries.

Mitigation options (ordered by speed):
1) Emergency policy rollback for the reserve-tightening change (low-risk, immediate).
2) Temp increase to Eidos’ burst-credit allocation + priority routing to their dedicated pool (requires config push, ~20–30m).
3) Longer-term: tune the sliding-window threshold and add an exception rule for reserved customers with sustained-surge profiles.

I attached rl-policy-diff.patch (the change) and a short runbook pointer for the rollback. I'll stand by for the go-ahead.

Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus@redwood.com

Attachments: rl-policy-diff.patch, runbook_quota-emergency.md
